misleading_risk: Low if trimmed, with three real risks. (1) Seed fill: the READMEs describe the Python library or the whole repository, not always the installed desktop app. NucleiSky's OME-Zarr support is behind `pip install "nucleisky[all]"` (README:53) and docs/2D/data_preparation.md says "be ready to provide [pixel size] manually". If the seed manifests state "OME-Zarr" outright, the preview claims something no author confirmed for the app. (2) The label "Works with" collides with the existing "Works in", which means host programs: filter label at pages_apps.py:27 and Details row at :147. A visitor could read "Works with" as napari/Fiji. (3) A short list reads as exhaustive. "Accepts: TrackMate CSV or XML" hides the Custom notebook that takes CellProfiler, Icy, ilastik and Fiji Manual Tracker CSV (README:146-175; the seed lists only the two TrackMate notebooks). Mitigations: seed text only for statements the README makes about the app itself, in the file marked DRAFT for the owner; the live site reads only the app repositories; "Not stated by the app's authors" is accurate; the existing "Read more: Documentation" link stays below.
refined_proposal:
Build a smaller version of G1:

1. Schema (schema/labconstrictor-app.schema.json). Add three optional plain-text arrays, copying the `quickstart` pattern:
 - `inputs`: 1-3 items, 5-110 characters each.
 - `outputs`: 1-3 items, 5-110 characters each.
 - `limitations`: 1-3 items, 5-140 characters each.
 The caps are tighter than the auditor's 1-6 x 160. Six long items would push "Get it" off the first phone screen (it starts at 444 px on NucleiSky now), and a cap is what stops a README paste.
 Dimensionality goes into the `inputs` text (for example "2D images only, no z-stacks"). `limitations` holds caveats only.
 Do not add `example_data` in this change.

2. Render, with no new module. `pages_apps.py` is 208 lines and `page_app` is 20 lines, so adding about 25 lines and one `p.add(...)` stays inside the 300 and 30 limits. Add `glance_block(app)` between the header and "Get it".
 - It reuses the existing `<dl class="lc-facts">` with rows "Accepts" and "Produces". Do not call the first row "Works with", because that clashes with "Works in". Items go through `esc` and `optional_list`. A few CSS lines make the lists tight.
 - Add `limits_section(app)`: a short h2 "Limitations" list after "About", rendered only when the author wrote it. No placeholder and no warning, so authors are not pushed into filler and the site never implies "no limitations".
 - One shared predicate, `expects_facts(manifest, section)`, in validate.py next to `optional_list`. It is true for kinds analysis, segmentation, simulation and utility in the main section. It is false for the testing section and for kinds game and training.
 - For an expecting app with `inputs` or `outputs` absent, show "Not stated by the app's authors" in that row. For an exempt app, omit the rows. This matches the license and authors precedent.

3. Warning. In `catalogue.resolve`, one extra line appends `"inputs, outputs not stated: ..."` through a small pure helper when `expects_facts` is true and a field is missing. The helper is `warnings += ...`; `resolve` is 18 lines, so it stays well inside 30. This follows the icon-warning precedent in `read_icon`: the app stays listed. The warning reaches the submitter through `submit_app.py:58` and `build/problems.md`. `publish.yml:69` greps only the Problems section, so no daily issue is opened. Expected today: 4 warnings (NucleiSky, CellTracksColab, VLab4Mic, GuessTheCondition) until their owners write the fields.

4. Seed drafts (seed/manifests, DRAFT for the owners). Fill only what the README or docs say about that app, for example:
 - CellTracksColab: TrackMate CSV or XML; CellProfiler, Icy, ilastik and Fiji Manual Tracker CSV; limitation "does not yet support track merging or splitting" (README:248).
 - GuessTheCondition: TIFF (.tif/.tiff) in one folder per condition and repeat; outputs accuracy against chance, confusion matrix, decision times and a PDF report (README:14-35).
 - NucleiSky: two images with a correct µm/px pixel size; outputs transform JSON, aligned image (.tif or .zarr), overlay PNG (docs/exports.md); limitation "similarity transform only, no shear or elastic warp" (docs/limitations.md).
 Do not state OME-Zarr for the app unless the owner confirms it. The real values belong in each app's own labconstrictor-app.yaml.

5. Docs and tests. Add the pattern to DESIGN.md first, in the same change. Add 3 lines to the `content/submit.md` example. Tests in tests/test_catalogue.py and tests/test_site.py cover: present, absent for an expecting app (placeholder plus warning), absent for an exempt app (omitted, no warning), over-length (schema rejects), and `<b>`/`&` escaped.

6. Rollout and cross-repo changes.
 - Merge the site schema first. The site validates against its own copy, so an app adding fields earlier would be delisted and named in problems.md.
 - Then copy the schema into LabConstrictor_streamlit/schemas (a copy, per its README). Leave the initialiser form (`manifest_form.py`, `app_manifest.py`) for later: it exposes only name, summary, kind, hosts, description and icon today, not even `quickstart`.
 - Drop the auditor's "template app-manifest guide" item. The template checkout has no `.tools/schema/` and no manifest page in `.tools/docs`, so the author-facing documentation is `content/submit.md` plus the schema.
evidence:
Gap is real (checked built pages with Playwright and the code):
- Headings on all six built app pages (site/apps/*/index.html): "Get it, [Windows, macOS, Linux, Notebooks], About, Using it, All downloads, How to install, Details". No "Works with", "Produces" or "Limitation" text appears.
- Screenshots of /apps/nucleisky/ at 1280 and 390 px (scratchpad/skeptic-g1/) show only icon, name, summary, badges and the GitHub pill, then "Get it". "About" starts 1064 px down on desktop and 1624 px on phone.
- schema/labconstrictor-app.schema.json has `additionalProperties: false` and no inputs/outputs/limitations. I ran jsonschema on the NucleiSky snapshot manifest plus `inputs: ['TIFF']` and got: "Additional properties are not allowed ('inputs' was unexpected)".
- The only existing carrier is the free-text `description`, which does not state formats. NucleiSky: "finds the calibrated similarity transform that best overlaps two landmark constellations". CellTracksColab: "tracking results (for example from TrackMate)". Only GuessTheCondition and Playground say anything about outputs, and not input formats.
- The facts exist only in the app repositories. README line numbers (docs/*.md for NucleiSky):
  - CellTracksColab README:146-175 (format table: CSV or XML for TrackMate, CSV for Custom) and :248 ("does not yet support track merging or splitting").
  - NucleiSky docs/2D/data_preparation.md (TIFF/OME-TIFF recommended; Zarr, NPY, PNG with caveats), docs/limitations.md (2D only; similarity transform only) and docs/exports.md (transform JSON, aligned .tif/.zarr, overlay PNG).
  - GuessTheCondition README:27-35 (.tif/.tiff, folder per condition and repeat) and :14-22 (results).
  - Playground README:48 ("Honest limits").
- Only LabConstrictor-Playground has a labconstrictor-app.yaml in its repo. The other five are served from seed/manifests via --manifest-dir, so any filled seed text is our draft, not author text.

Proportionality and rule fit (checked):
- Optional fields are explicitly allowed by AGENTS.md, and `optional_list` (validate.py:34) exists for them.
- The proposal copies the `quickstart` pattern (array of 5-200 char strings, max 6).
- `resolve` is 18 lines (catalogue.py:91-108) and `page_app` is 20 lines (pages_apps.py:189-208), so one added line each is safe. Warnings are surfaced by `fetch_catalogue.py:39` and `submit_app.py:58` and do not open daily issues (`publish.yml:69`).
- Docs/template part of the auditor's claim is stale: LabConstrictor/.tools has no `schema/` and .tools/docs has no manifest guide (grep for "labconstrictor-app" returned nothing).
- The streamlit schema copy is byte-identical in content to the site's (diff via sorted JSON: SAME), so a one-file sync is enough.

Not verified: how the Playwright layout would look after the change (nothing was edited), and whether the desktop apps accept every format the library READMEs list.
